chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام: May I perform salat (prayer) while images are in front of me and I am looking at them? He said: There is no problem; cast a cloth over them. And there is no problem with them if they are on your right, or your left, or behind you, or beneath your feet, or above your head. But if they are in the qiblah direction, then throw a cloth over them and perform salat (prayer).

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلُ: images or statues present in the place of prayer
key_terms.ثَوْبًا: a cloth used here to cover the images
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no legal problem or objection

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) while images or statues are present in front of them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing salat (prayer) in the presence of images. It indicates that images do not invalidate salat (prayer) in general, especially when they are not directly in the qiblah direction, but if they are in front toward the qiblah, they should be covered.
